#Part 1
1.Open the sleep dataset in R
```{r}
data(sleep)
```

2. Is it long or wide format? How do you know?
#It is in long format as there are several rows for one participant 

3. Transform this data so that it is in the other format.
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(reshape2)

sleepDatWide <- pivot_wider(sleep, id_cols = "ID", names_from = "group", values_from = "extra")
```

4. Transform your data back to its original format.
```{r}
sleepDatLong <- pivot_longer(sleepDatWide, cols = c("1", "2"), names_to = "group", values_to = "extra")
```

5. Open the Starwars dataset
```{r}
data(starwars)
```

6. Create homeworld as a factor. How many levels does it have?
```{r}
class(starwars$homeworld)

starwars$homeworldTwo <- as.factor(starwars$homeworld)

levels(starwars$homeworldTwo)
#48, counted based on the output of levels

```

7. Reorder homeworld so that Naboo is the reference group.
```{r}
starwars$homeworldTwo <- relevel(starwars$homeworldTwo, ref= "Naboo")
levels(starwars$homeworldTwo)

```

8. Use mutate to create a column transforming kg to pounds. (hint: you may need to look up the conversion)
```{r}
newMass <- starwars %>% mutate(massLb = mass*2.205) %>% select(mass, massLb)

newMass
```

9. Print a summary of your column from #8
```{r}
summary(newMass)
#inlcudes original mass column as a comparision
```


#Part 2
10. open the billboard dataset.
```{r}
data(billboard)
```

11. are the data in this dataframe in long or wide format? explain how you know.
#The data are in wide format there is one row per song and several columns for each week.

12. change the data from its original format to the other version.
```{r}
billboardLong <- pivot_longer(billboard, cols = colnames(billboard)[4:79], names_to = "week", values_to = "rank on top 100", values_drop_na = TRUE)

```

13. change it from your altered version in #3 back to its original state.
```{r}
billboardWide <- pivot_wider(billboardLong, id_cols = c("artist", "track", "date.entered"), names_from = "week", values_from = "rank on top 100")
```

14. Separate the date entered column into three columns: one for year, one for month, and one for day.
```{r}
billboard %>% separate(date.entered, into = c("year", "month", "day"), sep = "-")
```
